round_2_decisions: object 0.37.3 exposes section bytes, not an FDE reader. Added a range-only bounded reader; no dependencies, manifests, Cargo.lock files, or crates/elohim-host-contract edits.

FDE reader supports DWARF32/64, CIE versions 1/3, empty or z/L/P/R/S augmentations, absolute and PC-relative pointer forms, fixed signed/unsigned widths and LEB128. Unsupported pointer applications, indirect FDE PCs, malformed lengths/references, and overflow refuse. CFI instructions are not needed to locate ranges. DWARF64 still uses 32-bit CIE IDs/pointers in .eh_frame; reviewed against locally cached gimli parser source, not added as a dependency.
A present symbol table is authoritative even when it contains no eligible functions. Zero-size functions label gaps but create no range. Sized symbols outside their executable section refuse.
Instruction decoding is bounded by each merged range. Invalid or truncated instructions name the address and containing symbol, or explicitly identify the absence of a symbol in an FDE-only range.
Coverage includes total, covered, uncovered bytes and at most five gaps per executable section with nearest preceding symbol. Unknown sections refuse together by name.

The previous current-executable round-trip test now uses a fully bounded synthetic ELF because real linker sections legitimately refuse under decision 3; captured real .eh_frame is separately tested to cover the test executable main.
Both measured known-range ISA closures are v3 plus extensions, not plain v3. There are no decoded AVX-512 features; no claim of a complete binary ISA clause is possible while unknown sections refuse.
